name: BF1_CAPACITY_EXT_K8_K32

quotes.decision_8_1_fixed: 本批 MF 主表固定 **K=16、temperature=1、ridge=0、W weight decay=0**。
quotes.decision_8_1_extension: 这是对原包 K×lr 网格的明确修改：先用共同 K16 回答机制问题。K8/K32 如用于自然图像，另记容量扩展，不暗中并入主表，也不增加没有入账的 27 格。
quotes.decision_9_4_design: 三个 MF 族增加 K8 和 K32，继承各自 K16 在独立调参套选定的 lr/cap；同为 2000 步、每 250 步 checkpoint，按该重复的 CAL 样本 U-J 选 checkpoint，不访问 oracle。使用相同 10 个 data seed 和算法 seed1001，不另加算法重复或调参网格。
quotes.decision_9_4_meaning: 其含义是**固定训练规则下的容量响应**，包含优化因素，不称为每个 K 独立充分优化后的最优容量曲线。

protocol_p2.bf_batch1.capacity_extension: K8 / K32 on natural images only as a separately named capacity extension, never mixed into the main table and never 27 unbudgeted cells
protocol_p2.t03.capacity.interpretation: capacity response under fixed training rules (includes optimisation effects); not an independently optimised capacity curve

authority.scope: The owner asked for the experiments to be completed and left the scope to the main session, which decided (2026-10-19) to run this separately named natural-image capacity extension, modelled on the T03 capacity block (decision 9.4): fixed training rule, hyperparameters inherited from K16, no new tuning grid, checkpoint chosen on each run's own CAL.

design_context: Designed on 2026-10-19 after the BF1 K16 CAL selections, the twelve K16 final DEV32/DEV24 readouts and the 1004/1005 seed replication had been seen. A secondary, separately named DEV capacity extension: not part of the BF1 primary table, not a confirmation, not an input to any method or K selection.
question: Under the fixed BF1 training rule, with each MF family's K16 CAL-selected learning rate (and M1 cap), how do DEV registration outcomes respond when the MF head width K is 8 or 32 instead of 16, paired by training seed with the existing K16 finals?
interpretation_scope: 固定训练规则下的容量响应 / capacity response under a fixed training rule: includes optimisation effects (learning rate and M1 cap tuned at K16; M1 solver convergence at a fixed cap; the same 3000 steps); not an optimal-capacity curve and not evidence about independently tuned K.

bf1_basis.use: scientific code imported only from this frozen tree; BF1 freeze(), GPU gate, runtime_check and checked_selection run in every job

MF_VCS_perm1.inherited: lr (and M1 cap) of the K16 CAL selection on tuning seed 1017; no K8/K32 candidate

MF_VCS_M0.inherited: lr (and M1 cap) of the K16 CAL selection on tuning seed 1017; no K8/K32 candidate

MF_VCS_M1.inherited: lr (and M1 cap) of the K16 CAL selection on tuning seed 1017; no K8/K32 candidate

K_reference.source: existing BF1 FINAL_DEV units of the same family and seed (not rerun)

pairing: Same algorithm seed => same host encoder initialisation (built before the head under torch.manual_seed(seed)), same HostBatchSampler stream (numpy default_rng(1000 + seed)): identical crops, positions and permutations at every K. Only the feature-map widths, W and everything they influence differ. Same L40S model; nodes may differ; CUDA kernels are not deterministic, so pairs are not bitwise replays.

tuning.rule: K8/K32 inherit the K16 selection; there are no K8/K32 tuning candidates (never 27 unbudgeted cells)

fixed_identical_to_bf1.optimizer: AdamW, one learning rate tied across encoders, feature maps and (perm1/M0) W
fixed_identical_to_bf1.M1: relative_zero_head: tau_b = 0.01 G_b(0), warm start from the previous batch W, W0 = 0, no floor, cap from the K16 selection
fixed_identical_to_bf1.reference: within-scene V, ordinary permutations including fixed points
fixed_identical_to_bf1.registration: unchanged R6-REG-P2 searcher; MF_VCS_perm1 J_perm1 energy, M0/M1 exact V moments; frozen encoder/feature/W pair
fixed_identical_to_bf1.precision: BF1 PROTOCOL precision settings and environment variables, enforced by BF1 runtime_check on NVIDIA L40S

k_override.only_change: BF1 run.config hard-codes TrainConfig(K=16); the capacity runner takes K from the unit identity
how_K_enters: TrainConfig.K -> Trainer: MFHead(16, 16, K, K) = per-side Linear(16, K) + softmax and W zeros(K, K)
perm1/M0: W in its own AdamW group (lr tied, decay 0), clipped with all parameters, projected to [-1, 1] after every step
M1: QuadraticHead/solve_box_head shapes follow the features (K x K); the zero-head reference, threshold and fp64-diagnostic trigger are K-independent
registration: MFRigidEnergy features_a/features_b of width K and W K x K; mf_energy_rows is width-generic
checkpoints: K-shaped state dicts loaded strictly; identity and CONFIG carry K
verification: run.py: dataclasses.asdict(capacity config) == BF1 config with only K replaced, at runtime for every unit
smoke_k.py (CPU Slurm, FIT data through the DataGuard): one real training step per family at K8/K16/K32
k_override.resume_fix: BF1 run.load_checkpoint used with map_location='cpu' (only token changed); step log cut to the checkpoint on resume

selection_rule.scope: each run on its own CAL (8 cores x 10 perturbations at each of the 12 checkpoints)
selection_rule.items: 1-4 of the common rule (item 5, candidate order, is constant within a run)

evaluation.DEV32: 32 DEV cores x 10 perturbations, only at the selected checkpoint

DEV24.rule: exclude DEV cores whose TMA position occurs in the included FIT or CAL roles

hardware.k16_reference_nodes: node52 and node57 (L40S); K8/K32 may run on any non-excluded L40S node

execution.submission: by the main session after review, in the frozen unit order (bundle SUBMISSION.json)
execution.why_one_job_per_unit: per-unit limits of 1.5 h / 3 h keep backfill short and isolate failures; a family-K job with three sequential seeds would need 4.5-9 h limits

budget.unit: allocated L40S GPU-seconds (1 GPU per job), from the Slurm StartTime

k16_measured_basis.note: BF1 receipts = node end clock - controller StartTime; node57 lagged the controller (~90 s), so its receipts were low; corrected = recorded + lag + median unlagged startup.

k_scaling_basis.argument: K enters only the per-side Linear(16, K) feature maps, the K x K head W and the head moments; the host encoders (K-independent) dominate every training step and every registration energy. T02 measured train-step time at K8/K16/K32 within 0.4% (perm1, M0) and 1.2% (M1 at a fixed 30 iterations), and the moments registration energy within 2.7% (K32). perm1 registration has a smaller K-dependent part (O(CNK), moments O(CNK^2)), so the moments ratio bounds it. The unbounded quantity is the M1 relative-rule iteration count per batch, which may change with K; it is bounded by the inherited cap 100 (K16 finals: mean 77-82 iterations, 10-16% of batches at the cap).

8.pessimistic_rule: max over K16 seeds of training x max(1, T02 K ratio) + remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

32.pessimistic_rule: max over K16 seeds of training x max(1, T02 K ratio) + remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

8.pessimistic_rule: max over K16 seeds of training x max(1, T02 K ratio) + remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

32.pessimistic_rule: max over K16 seeds of training x max(1, T02 K ratio) + remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

8.pessimistic_rule: every one of the 3000 batches at the iteration cap 100 (fit of step time on mean iterations per interval, max over K16 seeds) x max(1, T02 K ratio) + max K16 remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

32.pessimistic_rule: every one of the 3000 batches at the iteration cap 100 (fit of step time on mean iterations per interval, max over K16 seeds) x max(1, T02 K ratio) + max K16 remainder x max(1, registration ratio)

budget.admission_rule: At each job start, under one bundle lock: committed = sum over every other job of this extension of its receipt allocated seconds if it has exited, else its reservation (Slurm limit + 120 s) if admitted, else 300 s; the job runs only if committed + its own reservation <= the ceiling. Otherwise the unit is marked INCOMPLETE_BUDGET_CEILING (budget/<unit>.json) and the job exits 3.
budget.refused_unit_rule: A unit refused only because of outstanding reservations may be resubmitted after those jobs exit; it is final INCOMPLETE_BUDGET_CEILING if refused when no other job of the extension is running. Resubmission never depends on CAL/DEV results.
budget.resume_rule: A unit interrupted by its time limit or infrastructure may be resubmitted once, unconditionally on results, subject to admission; it resumes from its last verified checkpoint (step log cut to that step, checkpoint deserialised on CPU). A second interruption leaves the unit INCOMPLETE.
budget.never_extended: No time limit, ceiling, step count or seed is increased after any CAL/DEV result is seen.

qc: all 3000 training steps logged exactly once (verify_result)
DEV32 = 320 rows at the selected checkpoint; DEV24 = 240 rows / 24 cores
CONFIG.K equals the unit K; lr/cap equal the inherited selection
every ENV: NVIDIA L40S, partition L40S, BF1 precision settings
data reads only FIT/CAL/DEV through the DataGuard; TEST134 and EPFL never read
all artifact hashes recorded in COMPLETE.json verified
exit receipt exit_code 0 for the completing job
test_repeat: TEST_REPEAT remains HOLD. This extension is not an input to any method or K selection; any held-out use of K8/K32 would need its own pre-registration before images are read.

reporting.table: BF1 capacity extension (fixed training rule): separate table, never merged into the BF1 main table or the seed-replication table
reporting.rows: family x K in {8, 16 (existing paired BF1 finals, reference), 32}
per_unit: M1: fraction of batches at the cap, median iterations
reporting.paired: per seed: K minus K16 of the same family and seed; seed mean
reporting.incomplete: a family-K cell with fewer than 3 complete seeds is reported as INCOMPLETE with its available seeds only

statistics.primary_metric: DEV32 success42 (as the BF1 primary readout)
statistics.contrast: Delta_s = metric(K, seed s) - metric(K16, seed s), s in 1001..1003; Delta_bar = mean over seeds
statistics.uncertainty: success rates: core-cluster bootstrap of Delta_bar using per-core success fractions (each core keeps its 10 perturbations), B = 10000 resamples of the 32 (DEV24: 24) cores with replacement, numpy default_rng(20261019), percentile 95% interval; seeds are not resampled (n = 3, shown individually); median error: per-seed paired differences only
statistics.multiplicity: 3 families x 2 K x 2 rates x 2 core sets, descriptive; no family-wise error control and no significance wording

interpretation_grid.applies_to: each family x K, DEV32 success42 primary; the same grid is reported descriptively for success9 and DEV24
interpretation_grid.A_consistent_response: the 95% interval excludes 0 and all three Delta_s share its sign (none zero): "K differs from K16 under the fixed training rule (includes optimisation effects)", with the direction
interpretation_grid.B_no_detectable_response: the 95% interval includes 0: "no capacity response detectable at this sample size under the fixed rule"
interpretation_grid.C_mixed: the interval excludes 0 but the three Delta_s disagree in sign or one is 0: "mixed: core-level difference not consistent across seeds"
interpretation_grid.all_outcomes: no optimal-K claim; the BF1 K16 main table, its selections and the method comparison rules (decision 5) are unchanged

forbidden_claims: merging K8/K32 into the BF1 main table or ranking families with them
completed matrix when any unit is INCOMPLETE
limitations: 3 training seeds; DEV is a development benchmark (32 cores; perturbations are not independent cores)
designed after K16 DEV readouts were seen (see design_context)
CAL is saturated for many K16 checkpoints (success42 = success9 = 1), so the checkpoint choice is driven by the median error
K16 hyperparameters may favour K16; a K8/K32 difference can reflect optimisation, not capacity alone
